facts.statement: The genus Pseudocorax was described by Priem in 1897.
The type species of the genus is Pseudocorax affinis.

Six other species are recognized within the genus, including Pseudocorax heteromorphus, Pseudocorax laevis, Pseudocorax granti, Pseudocorax duchaussoisi, Pseudocorax kindlimanni, and Pseudocorax heteroserratus.
facts.quote: subdivision: †Pseudocorax heteromorphus (Reuss, 1845) †Pseudocorax laevis Leriche, 1906 †Pseudocorax granti Cappetta & Case, 1975 †Pseudocorax duchaussoisi Guinot, Underwood, Cappetta, & Ward, 2013 †Pseudocorax kindlimanni Jambura, Stumpf, & Kriwet, 2021 †Pseudocorax heteroserratusEgli, Goode, Rempert & Rego, 2025

facts.statement: The genus Pseudocorax contains six valid species.
Pseudocorax was formerly placed in the family Anacoracidae but is now classified in its own family, Pseudocoracidae, alongside Galeocorax.
facts.quote: It was formerly assigned to the family Anacoracidae, but is now placed in its own family Pseudocoracidae along with Galeocorax

facts.statement: The parent group of the genus Pseudocorax is the family Pseudocoracidae.
Pseudocorax belongs to the class Chondrichthyes.
The time range for Pseudocorax spans from the Aptian to the Bartonian, between 119.57 and 37.71 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Bartonian (119.57 to 37.71 million years ago)

facts.statement: Fossils of Pseudocorax have been found in Europe, the Middle East, North Africa, and North America.
facts.quote: It contains six valid species that have been found in Europe, the Middle East, North Africa, and North America

facts.statement: The species formerly known as Pseudocorax australis and Pseudocorax primulus have been reidentified as species of Echinorhinus and Squalicorax, respectively.
facts.quote: The former species "P." australis and "P." primulus have been reidentified as species of Echinorhinus and Squalicorax, respectively

facts.statement: There are 81 recorded fossil occurrences of Pseudocorax.

rejected.statement: Pseudocorax was an extinct genus of mackerel sharks that lived during the Late Cretaceous.
rejected.quote: Pseudocorax is an extinct genus of mackerel sharks that lived during the Late Cretaceous
